 Last Updated On Oct 29, 2026 | 23:40 IST

 amul protein teaser Summary Amul will launch a high-protein savoury snack on October 30, expanding its protein push beyond dairy into the snack aisle. The company says the product took over a year of research and development and is designed to deliver protein comparable to a scoop of protein powder while keeping calories in check. Its nutritional details, price and flavours are yet to be disclosed.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source Amul is taking its protein play to the snack aisle. The dairy major is set to launch a high-protein savoury snack on Friday, October 30, with a brand manager claiming that its protein content and calories will be comparable to those of a scoop of protein powder.
 Shefali Vijaywargiya, a brand manager at Amul, announced the upcoming launch in a post on X on Thursday, revealing that the product took more than a year of research and development (R&D) to get right.
 The brief was to pack a meaningful amount of protein into each serving while keeping calories in check — a combination the company hopes will make nutritious snacking more convenient. The product is designed for on-the-go consumption and can also be customised to suit individual preferences, Vijaywargiya said.
 Launching tomorrow!
At Amul, we have been on a mission to help Indians meet their daily protein needs, with a target of at least 1 g of protein per kg of body weight every day.
With a wide range of high protein products across categories, we are now setting our sights on a new category to help build another daily protein habit: savoury snacks.
Our challenge was to make snacking functional by delivering meaningfully high protein per serving, using the best quality protein, and keeping calories in check so that protein-rich snacking could become part of the daily diet.
It was a difficult brief. After over a year of R&D, we are excited to have cracked it!
A high protein snack with calories and protein comparable to a scoop of protein powder!
Designed for convenient on-the-go snacking yet versatile enough for you to personalise and discover your own favourite ways to enjoy it.
We’re excited about what we’ve created. Stay tuned!
— Shefali Vijaywargiya (@Shefali_Vj) October 29, 2026 Amul looks beyond dairy for its protein push 
 The launch marks Amul’s planned entry into savoury snacks as it seeks to make protein consumption a more regular part of Indian diets. The company has been working towards a target of at least 1 gram of protein per kilogram of body weight per day, according to Vijaywargiya.
 Its latest offering extends that ambition beyond its existing portfolio of protein-focused products into a category that consumers can incorporate into their daily routines.
 However, the comparison with protein powder remains a claim from the brand manager, rather than a verified nutritional assessment. Amul has yet to disclose the snack’s exact protein content, calorie count, ingredients or serving size.
 The product’s name, flavours, price and availability are also awaited. These details will help establish how it compares with competing packaged snacks and whether its nutritional proposition comes at a price consumers are willing to pay.
 With the launch scheduled for Friday, Amul’s challenge will be to translate its protein pitch into a snack that delivers on taste, convenience and affordability — without making everyday snacking feel like a workout.
